newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end dismal week at new 6-1/3 yr low.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end dismal week at new 6-1/3 yr low.

text.p: The Thai stock market continued to take a beating on Friday and although some local fund buying helped pare losses the key index ended the week down 8.3 percent at a new 6-1/3 year low.
The composite SET index ended the day off 8.63 points, or 1.41 percent, at 605.43. The SET 50 closed 0.67 points or 1.49 percent lower at 44.35. Turnover was a modest 2.44 billion baht.
Local funds bought blue chips shares during the afternoon and kept the market in the 600-605 range, traders said.
In the morning heavy foreign selling of finance and bank stocks had briefly taken the index below the 600-point level.
"I think some local funds were coming in as the market is so low and buying back stocks sold earlier in the day. I think the foreigners keep selling," said a broker at Cathay Capital.

Concerns surrounding the currency, economic growth prospects, high interest rates, export performance, corporate earnings, liquidity and finance sector mergers continue to unnerve investors, traders said.
Currency worries resurfaced following reports that the central bank intervened in the Singapore forex market this morning after the baht came under speculative attack.
Talk that a planned merger between Thai Danu Bank Plc and Finance One Plc was in trouble continued to circulate, traders said. Thai Danu denied the talk and said the merger was still continuing.

"It was the same old news in the market today. There were a few nerves about the baht after the intervention this morning and the Thai Danu merger is also affecting the market," said another local broker.
